title: The High Court and the Constitution
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the High Court's role in interpreting the Constitution and striking down laws beyond parliament's power; the first covers which rights the Constitution protects and the second covers courts and NGOs in environmental law.

draft.title: The High Court and the Constitution
card: The High Court of Australia is the final court of appeal. It also interprets the Constitution, which sets out the powers of the Commonwealth Parliament.
The Commonwealth Parliament can only make laws on topics the Constitution gives it. A law outside those powers is invalid.
If someone challenges a law, the High Court decides whether it is within power. It can strike down a law that is not, so the law has no effect.
The High Court also protects representative government. It has found that the Constitution implies a freedom of political communication, which lets people discuss political matters.
draft.remember: The High Court checks parliament by striking down laws made outside the Constitution.

a.q: What can the High Court do if the Commonwealth Parliament passes a law outside its constitutional power?
opts: Strike the law down so it has no effect
Amend the law so that it fits the Constitution
Send the law back to parliament to be voted on again
Ask the Governor-General to repeal the law
a.why: The High Court interprets the Constitution and can declare a law invalid. Amending a law is tempting, but that is a job for parliament, not a court.
a.clue: Think about what a court can do to an invalid law.

b.q: A business owner in Geelong challenges a Commonwealth law, arguing that it covers a topic the Constitution does not give parliament power over. Which body decides whether the law is valid?
opts: The High Court, by interpreting the Constitution
The Commonwealth Parliament, by reviewing its own law
The Governor-General, by refusing to sign the law
The Victorian Supreme Court, by amending the law
b.why: The High Court decides if a law is within the Constitution and can strike it down if not. Parliament made the law, so it does not rule on its own validity.

a.best: Strike the law down so it has no effect

b.best: The High Court, by interpreting the Constitution
